plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with slender gray-green leaves and dense spikes of small tubular flowers. It is widely cultivated in gardens and in commercial fields for essential oils, and it attracts bees and butterflies in great numbers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June to August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the western Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Tasmania, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans used lavender to scent their baths.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large composite flower head made up of a central disk of tiny florets surrounded by showy yellow ray petals. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, a behavior called heliotropism.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midsummer to early fall in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; widely farmed in Ukraine, Russia, Argentina, and the central United States
plants.funFact: The spiral pattern of seeds in the sunflower head follows the Fibonacci sequence, which packs the seeds as efficiently as possible.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial that raises large, fragrant flowers on tall stalks above round, water-repellent leaves. It grows in shallow ponds and slow-moving waters, and is culturally important across Asia as a symbol of purity.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, peaking in July and August in temperate Asia
plants.location: Native to Asia and Australia; cultivated in India, China, Japan, Vietnam, and in ponds around the world
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a microscopic surface structure that makes water bead up and roll off, carrying dirt away. This is known as the 'lotus effect' and has inspired self-cleaning materials.

plants.name: Eucalyptus caesia
plants.description: A small, graceful mallee-type eucalypt with powdery white-silver bark and weeping branches. Its large, showy flowers appear in the Southern Hemisphere winter and provide nectar for native birds and insects when little else blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter, roughly May to August in Australia
plants.location: Native to granite outcrops in Western Australia; grown in gardens in mild climates
plants.funFact: This species grows naturally only on a few granite outcrops in Western Australia, yet it is a popular ornamental tree around the world.
